prompt: An object P undergoes uniform circular motion. In the diagram, P is at the left of the circle and its centre is to the right of P; arrow W points left, X points up, Y points right (towards the centre) and Z points down. Which arrow shows the direction of the net force acting on P?
hint: For uniform circular motion the net force is centripetal: directed towards the centre of the circle.

prompt: For an object in uniform circular motion, the net force is always directed towards the centre of the circle and is perpendicular to the object's velocity.
hint: The speed is constant, so the net force does no work; it only changes the direction of the velocity.

prompt: Which of the following provides evidence for the wave model of light proposed by Huygens?
hint: Diffraction (bending of light around edges and through gaps) is a wave behaviour; the other three are explained by treating light as photons.

prompt: Which of the following is a fundamental particle in the Standard Model of matter?
hint: The photon is a fundamental force-carrying particle. Hadrons (including the proton and neutron) are made of quarks.

prompt: A photon is a fundamental particle, but a proton is not, because a proton is made of quarks.
hint: A proton is two up quarks and one down quark held together by gluons.

prompt: A coil mounted on an axle in a uniform magnetic field rotates continuously (acts as a motor) when it is connected to a ___ supply through a ___.
hint: The commutator reverses the current in the coil every half turn so the torque keeps acting the same way around.

prompt: Without a split-ring commutator, a coil carrying a steady direct current in a uniform magnetic field would turn only until its plane is perpendicular to the field, then stop (or oscillate), rather than rotating continuously.
hint: The torque drops to zero when the coil's plane is perpendicular to the field, and would then act to push it back.

prompt: Three star clusters X, Y and Z are shown as Hertzsprung-Russell diagrams. Cluster Y's main sequence still reaches the hot, luminous end; cluster X's main sequence turns off at a moderate point; cluster Z's turns off low, with a large giant branch. Order the three clusters from youngest to oldest.
hint: The lower on the main sequence a cluster's turnoff point is, the older the cluster, because the most massive stars have already evolved off the main sequence.

prompt: The 'main-sequence turnoff' point on a star cluster's Hertzsprung-Russell diagram moves to lower luminosity and cooler temperature as the cluster ages.
hint: More massive (hotter, brighter) stars run out of fuel first and leave the main sequence, so the turnoff creeps down over time.

prompt: The photoelectric effect is modelled by $K_{max} = hf - \phi$. In this equation the symbol $\phi$ represents the energy ___.
bank: required to release an electron from the material
supplied by a photon to an electron
retained by an electron after it is hit
left over after a photon-electron collision
answer: required to release an electron from the material
hint: $\phi$ is the work function: the minimum energy needed to free an electron from the metal's surface.

prompt: A pure sample of polonium-210 (half-life 138 days) decays by alpha emission to the stable isotope lead-206. After 276 days (two half-lives), the ratio of polonium-210 atoms to lead-206 atoms in the sample is ___.
hint: After two half-lives, one quarter of the polonium remains and three quarters has become lead.

prompt: A sample of polonium-210 has a half-life of 138 days. Calculate the fraction of the original polonium-210 that remains after 276 days.
hint: 276 days is two half-lives.

prompt: An ideal transformer gives an output of 6 V for an input of 240 V. To get an output of 12 V from the same 240 V input, you would ___ the number of turns on the primary coil (changing the load resistance would not work).
hint: The output voltage must double, so the secondary-to-primary turns ratio must double; halving the primary turns achieves this.

prompt: An ideal transformer steps 240 V down to 6 V. If the primary coil has 800 turns, calculate the number of turns on the secondary coil.
hint: $\dfrac{N_s}{N_p} = \dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{6}{240}$.

prompt: Object P is dropped from rest and object Q is launched horizontally from the same height at the same instant. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement correctly compares their motion?
options: The final speed of Q is greater than the final speed of P
The acceleration of P is less than the acceleration of Q
The time of flight of Q is greater than the time of flight of P
The initial vertical velocity of P is less than the initial vertical velocity of Q
answer: The final speed of Q is greater than the final speed of P
hint: Both have acceleration g downward, the same time of flight and the same vertical velocity at landing; but Q also has a horizontal velocity component, so its final speed is larger.

prompt: An object dropped from rest and an object launched horizontally from the same height reach the ground at the same time.
hint: The vertical motion (free fall from the same height) is identical for both; the horizontal motion does not affect the fall time.

prompt: A current-carrying rod is perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field and feels the maximum force F. Using $F = BIL\sin\theta$, through what angle must the rod be rotated so that the force becomes $\dfrac{F}{2}$?
hint: Half the maximum force needs $\sin\theta = 0.5$, so $\theta = 30^{\circ}$ from the field; that is a rotation of $60^{\circ}$ from the perpendicular position.

prompt: For a satellite in a circular orbit, the orbital speed v is ___ proportional to the square root of the orbital radius r.
hint: $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}$, so $v \propto r^{-1/2}$: a larger orbit means a slower satellite.

prompt: A rod has proper length $L_0$ (measured in its own frame). It travels past a stationary observer at speed v. On a graph of measured length against speed, four curves W, X, Y and Z all start at $L_0$ when v = 0. Which curve correctly shows how the observer's measured length depends on v?
options: X (length decreases, slowly at first then steeply as v approaches c)
Y (length decreases roughly in a straight line)
Z (length decreases steeply at first then levels off)
answer: X (length decreases, slowly at first then steeply as v approaches c)
hint: $L = L_0\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$: near v = 0 the effect is tiny, but the length falls sharply towards zero as v approaches c.

prompt: A rod of proper length 2.0 m travels past an observer at 0.6c. Calculate the length the observer measures. Use $L = L_0\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$.

Two identical satellites A and B orbit a planet. A is in the outer (larger) circular orbit and B is in the inner (smaller) orbit. Which row correctly compares their gravitational potential energy U and kinetic energy K?
hint: $U = -\dfrac{GMm}{r}$ (less negative, so larger, for the outer satellite) and $K = \dfrac{GMm}{2r}$ (smaller for the outer satellite).

prompt: A satellite in a higher circular orbit has a greater (less negative) gravitational potential energy but a smaller kinetic energy than an identical satellite in a lower orbit.
hint: Its total energy is also greater (less negative) than that of the lower satellite.

prompt: A proton travels at twice the speed of an alpha particle. The alpha particle has about 4 times the mass of the proton. If the proton's de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda$, the alpha particle's de Broglie wavelength is ___.
hint: $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$. The alpha particle's $mv$ is $4 \times \tfrac{1}{2} = 2$ times the proton's, so its wavelength is half.

prompt: A straight conductor rotates at a constant rate about one end, in the plane of the page, with a uniform magnetic field directed into the page (perpendicular to the plane of rotation). Over one revolution the EMF induced between its ends is ___.
bank: alternating between positive and negative peaks
hint: Every part of the rod sweeps area at the same steady rate, so the rate of change of flux does not change: $arepsilon = 	frac{1}{2}B\omega L^2$.

prompt: A rod of length 0.30 m rotates at an angular velocity of 20 rad s$^{-1}$ about one end, in a uniform magnetic field of 0.50 T directed perpendicular to the plane of rotation. Calculate the EMF induced between the ends of the rod, using $\varepsilon = \tfrac{1}{2}B\omega L^2$.
hint: $\varepsilon = 0.5 \times 0.50 \times 20 \times 0.30^2$.

prompt: The graph shows maximum photoelectron kinetic energy against incident photon energy for four metals, with threshold (x-intercept) values of about: K 2.1 eV, Li 2.4 eV, Mg 3.6 eV, Ag 4.5 eV. Light of frequency $7 \times 10^{14}$ Hz (photon energy about 2.9 eV) shines on all four metals. From which metals are photoelectrons emitted?
hint: A metal emits photoelectrons only if the photon energy exceeds its work function (threshold energy).

prompt: Calculate the energy, in electronvolts, of a photon of light with frequency $7 \times 10^{14}$ Hz. Use $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}$ J s and $1$ eV $= 1.60 \times 10^{-19}$ J.
hint: $E = hf$, then divide by $1.60 \times 10^{-19}$ to convert joules to eV.

prompt: In a cyclotron, a charged particle spirals outward, gaining speed. An electric field acts across the gap between the two D-shaped electrodes (dees), and a strong magnetic field is present everywhere. Which statement about the particle is true?
options: It undergoes acceleration both inside the dees and in the gap between them
It increases speed while inside the dees
It only accelerates while in the gap between the dees
It slows down inside the dees and speeds up in the gap
answer: It undergoes acceleration both inside the dees and in the gap between them
hint: In the gap the electric field speeds it up (linear acceleration); inside the dees the magnetic field bends its path in a circle (centripetal acceleration) at constant speed.

prompt: Inside the dees of a cyclotron the particle's speed does not change, but it is still accelerating because its direction of motion is continuously changing.
hint: Circular motion is accelerated motion even at constant speed.

prompt: A vacuum chamber contains a uniform electric field and a uniform magnetic field. A proton entering with velocity v travels straight through without any change in velocity. A second proton then enters at the same point, in the same direction, but with velocity 2v. In the chamber, the acceleration of the second proton:
options: changes in both magnitude and direction
is constant in magnitude and direction
is constant in magnitude but not in direction
answer: changes in both magnitude and direction
hint: The first proton is at the velocity-selector speed (electric and magnetic forces balance). The second, being faster, feels a larger magnetic force than electric force, so there is a net force; as its path curves, the magnetic force changes direction too.

prompt: In a region with crossed electric and magnetic fields (a velocity selector), only a charged particle moving at the speed $v = \dfrac{E}{B}$ passes straight through; a faster particle is deflected.
hint: At $v = E/B$ the electric and magnetic forces are equal and opposite; at any other speed they do not balance.

prompt: Three identical atomic clocks tick at the same rate when at rest. One stays in a laboratory X on Earth's equator (moving with Earth's rotation). One is on a satellite Y in a 12-hour circular orbit; one is on a satellite Z in a geostationary orbit. Considering only the effects of special relativity, and as measured by the observer at X, which statement is correct?
options: The clock at Y ticks slower than either the clock at X or the clock at Z
The clock at Y ticks faster than either the clock at X or the clock at Z
The clocks tick at different rates, with X the fastest and Y the slowest
The clocks tick at different rates, with Z the slowest and X the fastest
answer: The clock at Y ticks slower than either the clock at X or the clock at Z
hint: The satellite in the lower (12-hour) orbit moves fastest of the three, and the faster a clock moves relative to the observer, the more slowly it ticks.

prompt: According to special relativity, a clock moving relative to an observer runs slow compared with the observer's own clock, and the faster it moves the greater the effect.
hint: This is time dilation, described by the Lorentz factor.
